prerequisite: Boundaries must be closed (or snap-closed with coincident end points) and carry an elevation (Elevation = starting elevation z0); target_z above z0 = island closing upward, below z0 = pit closing downward
fixture_requirements: >= 2 closed LWPOLYLINEs with non-zero Elevation (one island and one pit, verifying both directions)
At least one with arc segments and concave corners (verifies the branch where a concave boundary offset splits into several rings)
At least one snap-closed pseudo-open line: Closed=false but end points coincide (verifies IsSnapClosed normalisation)
One deliberately small boundary with a far target_z (verifies early termination on collapse, collapsed=true)
assertions: In-memory change only: results must be kept with an explicit save_dwg
Zero rings means throw: when rings_total == 0 report the boundary count / open count / same-elevation count; an ok:true empty run is forbidden
The boundaries handle array takes precedence over layer; a handle that is not a polyline or does not exist throws and names the handle
A layer with no polylines throws and names the layer; open lines are skipped and counted in skipped_open
Every ring's Elevation is in {z0 +/- k*dz} union {target_z}; the last ring is always target_z (unless collapsed)
Offsets always go inward: every ring's area is strictly smaller than the previous one (island and pit alike; direction is decided by trial offsets on both sides)
All rings produced by a concave-boundary split are kept and share the same elevation (ring_handles count >= rings count)
Generated rings sit on the source boundary layer (Layer == src.Layer); source boundaries are untouched
With fillet_r > 0 the output rings contain arcs (CountArcs > 0); with fillet_r = 0 no smoothing or rounding
fillet_r defaults to round(2*n*dz, 3) (the horizontal step of two rings)
Collapsing boundaries: reached stops at the last successful ring, collapsed=true is visible in per_boundary, no throw, other boundaries unaffected
target_z equal to the boundary elevation skips that boundary and counts it in skipped_same_elevation
Missing target_z / slope_n throws; slope_n <= 0, step_dz <= 0, fillet_r < 0 throws
Ring geometry matches the products\waterbox command C3DF-OffsetCone(YT) on the same drawing and parameters (same OffsetConeCore)
